What we shared on the call:

- Peak traffic: ~650 RPS for short inputs during peak; typical <200 RPS.

3) Private/VPC: do you support a full air-gapped on-prem deployment or is it a VPC peering model with control plane in your cloud?

Hi Amelia — great talking earlier, thanks for the clear numbers. Short recap tailored to your three questions below; attaching a one-pager and our Dedicated SLA for reference.

Quick comparison (summary):
- Hosted API (fastest path)
  - Multi-tenant serving: application-level isolation, logical rate limiting, and per-customer request routing.
  - Isolation tradeoffs: compute is multiplexed across tenants. We use continuous batching and KV cache heuristics to reduce cross-tenant interference; in practice p95 impact is rare, but hard SLO guarantees on shared hosts are limited.
  - Best for: teams that prioritize time-to-market and cost.

- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools)
  - Single-tenant GPU pools assigned to the customer. No compute eviction from other customers (i.e., no noisy-neighbor compute interference).
  - You still share some cluster-level services (network fabric, storage backplanes) depending on configuration; we offer options to isolate networking and quota controls.
  - Best for: predictable throughput and tighter SLOs.

- Private (VPC / on-prem)
  - VPC option: customer-managed VPC with private control plane; we can also provide an on-prem appliance for air-gapped needs.
  - Strongest data isolation and compliance posture, but higher setup time and ops coordination.

Attachments included: redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf (SLA + maintenance window policy), deployment-options-summary.xlsx (feature/matrix).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Tessa (solutions engineer) + our SRE to discuss isolation, observability hooks (per-route latency metrics), and a sample canary/fallback strategy.
2) If Dedicated looks right, we can provision a 2-week proof-of-performance run to verify p95 at your peak traffic.
3) Procurement can review the attached SLA and draft; Marissa -> coordinate timelines.

Hi Amelia — looping in technical notes so the TD can be focused. Tessa and I will run through these items with concrete configs/examples. Short answers + pointers below.

1) Hosted production signals
- We have multiple customers (finserv + commerce) on Hosted serving p95s in the 80–140ms range depending on model/token distribution. We can share anonymized perf traces in the TD. Important caveat: Hosted uses multi-tenant GPU scheduling and batching which means worst-case latency SLOs are probabilistic rather than contractual.

2) Dedicated maintenance/eviction
- Dedicated = reserved GPU pools (VMs/instances pinned to your tenancy). We do not preempt customer GPUs for other tenants. Maintenance can require rolling restarts of nodes; we offer configurable maintenance windows and a live-evacuation workflow that shifts traffic to standby nodes in the pool.
- For extra protection we can provision a small hot-standby capacity to absorb rolling restarts without p95 degradation. This is standard for enterprise Dedicated contracts. See attached private-vpc-setup-guide.pdf for examples.

3) Failover behavior between Dedicated and Hosted
- Yes: you can configure automatic fallback routing. Our routing policy supports: primary=Dedicated, fallback=Hosted (with maxQPS and throttling caps). When failover occurs we annotate traces and can enforce per-route throttles to prioritize latency-sensitive calls.

Observability primitives we will demo in the TD
- Per-request trace IDs + distributed spans (sampled), token-level billing traces, per-route latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99), cache hit/miss metrics, and request queue/backlog gauges.

Suggested agenda for TD (60–75m)
- 10m: finalize peak profile and constraints (you)
- 25m: deep-dive on Dedicated topology, maintenance, and hot-standby options (Tessa + SRE)
- 20m: routing/failover demo + observability review (Tessa)
- 10m: open Q&A / next steps (setup PoP)

We can run Tue 2026-03-02 10:00 PST; I’ll send a calendar invite and a short pre-read that includes anonymized Hosted perf traces and a Dedicated runbook.
